issues.t: Front crossmember rust lets control arm detach (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, wandering steering, or a front wheel that suddenly tucks in because the lower control arm has broken free.
issues.why: Road salt rots the front crossmember where the lower control arms bolt on. Recall 16V-458 covers 2002-2007 Lancers and 2003-2006 Evolutions, and recall 20V-279 covers 2008-2010 Lancers, in salt-belt states. CarComplaints owners also report rotted subframes.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer inspects the crossmember and seals or replaces it free. Get any front-end clunk checked before driving far.

issues.sym: A "slow down" or transmission warning with the check engine light, shudder or surging when pulling away, revs flaring, or loss of drive.
issues.why: The CVT can overheat or let its belt slip, and early cars also had control module faults. A 2021 class action covers 2014-2017 Lancers, and Mitsubishi bulletin 20-23-001 tells dealers to replace the valve body or the CVT.
issues.next: Pull over and let it cool if the warning appears. Have the CVT fluid and codes checked, and ask a dealer whether the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty (original owners) covers it.

issues.sym: No symptoms until a crash. In a crash, the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: Takata passenger airbag inflators can degrade from moisture over time (recalls 17V-569 and 18V-220, which also replaced some earlier interim inflators).
issues.next: Check your VIN now and get the free inflator replacement as soon as possible. Until then, don’t let anyone ride in the front passenger seat.

issues.t: Accessory drive belt can come off (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or slapping from the engine, then a battery light, heavy steering or rising temperature if the belt comes off. The engine may stall.
issues.why: Worn engine pulleys (recall 14V-562, 2008-2011 including Evolution and Ralliart) or a cracked belt tensioner flange (recall 18V-069, 2009-2012) can let the drive belt jump off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; the dealer replaces the tensioner, belt and worn pulleys free.

issues.sym: An AWC or AYC warning light, and the all-wheel-drive system no longer sends power between the wheels the way it should. The car may feel less stable in corners.
issues.why: The pump that runs the Active Center Differential and Active Yaw Control sits exposed behind the right rear wheel and corrodes. It is the most common Evolution X fault, especially on 2008-2010 cars, often around 50,000-60,000 miles.
issues.next: Drive gently until it is fixed. Ask a dealer whether the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty applies, and change the ACD/AYC fluid about every 30,000 miles.

issues.sym: Slipping or harsh engagement, especially when cold, jerky low-speed moves, or a transmission warning light.
issues.why: The 6-speed twin-clutch gearbox on the Ralliart and Evolution MR sheds metal particles that wear the clutch packs and damage the valve body. It also needs more frequent fluid service.
issues.next: Change the transmission fluid and filter on schedule. If it slips, get a specialist diagnosis quickly; ask whether the powertrain warranty still applies.

issues.sym: The clutch pedal goes soft or sinks, and you can’t shift into or out of gear.
issues.why: The clutch master cylinder on manual Evolution X cars can fail (recall 13V-446).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the master cylinder free.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch on turbo models
issues.sym: A check engine light for cam/crank timing, a rattle at startup, rough running, or in bad cases a no-start.
issues.why: The timing chain on the turbocharged 2.0L stretches over time, faster when oil changes are skipped.
issues.next: Change the oil on time with the right grade. If timing codes appear, have the chain checked before it jumps teeth.

issues.sym: A check engine light with code P0420, a failed emissions test, and sometimes a rattle or rotten-egg smell.
issues.why: The catalytic converter on these Lancers loses efficiency. Mitsubishi released a converter kit and a service bulletin that also calls for reprogramming the engine computer.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the code with live sensor data and ask the dealer about the bulletin and computer update before replacing the converter.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak and misfire
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine, a burning oil smell, or misfires and a check engine light.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket hardens with age and leaks oil, including into the spark plug wells, where it causes misfires.
issues.next: Replace the valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals, and clean the plug wells. Check the plugs and coils for oil damage.

issues.sym: White, cloudy patches on the paint, then the clear coat flakes off, usually on the hood, roof and trunk.
issues.why: The factory clear coat breaks down with sun exposure. RepairPal lists dozens of owner reports.
issues.next: Wash and wax regularly and park in shade. Once it peels, the panel has to be sanded and refinished.

issues.t: Temperature control knob hard to turn
issues.sym: The heater temperature knob gets stiff or sticks.
issues.why: The knob and the heater door linkage it moves stiffen with age. RepairPal lists more than 170 owner reports, and Mitsubishi has issued a service action.
issues.next: Don’t force the knob. Have a shop free up or replace the stuck knob or linkage.

issues.sym: Steam or mist from under the hood after highway driving, coolant on the ground, or the coolant level dropping.
issues.why: Owners reported leaking radiators around 35,000-50,000 miles, and in one case a radiator cap that no longer held pressure.
issues.next: Don’t drive if it overheats. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the radiator and cap replaced as needed.

issues.t: CVT whine or clicking from bad bearings
issues.sym: A whine, hum or clicking that gets louder as speed rises.
issues.why: Pulley-shaft bearings inside the CVT can fail. Bulletin 15-23-003 covers 2008-2010 Lancers.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the bulletin applies; the repair is covered by the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty for original owners.

issues.t: Brake pedal hard at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and the car takes longer to stop, mostly after long drives without braking.
issues.why: The check valve on the brake booster can stick closed and cut power assist (recall 09V-077).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the check valve free.

issues.sym: Often no symptoms, though the airbag (SRS) light may come on. In a crash the front airbags may deploy late.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the front impact sensors (recall 09V-435). Owners also report SRS lights on these years.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer installs corrosion-resistant sensors free. Get any SRS light diagnosed.

issues.sym: Wind noise or rattling from the sunroof, or the glass lifting or coming off while driving.
issues.why: The sunroof glass can detach from its frame (recall 18V-071).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the glass assembly free.

issues.t: Headlights, taillights or wipers act up (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights, taillights or wipers work erratically or stop.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the control unit for these lights and the wipers can cause unstable voltage (recall 15V-232).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the control unit free.

issues.sym: No air from the vents, only some fan speeds work, or the windshield won’t defrost.
issues.why: The blower motor can fail (recall 15V-233). On cars outside the recall, a failed blower speed resistor is a common cause.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Otherwise have the resistor tested before replacing the motor.

issues.t: Faulty relays can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, loses power or overheats without warning.
issues.why: Some relays in the engine compartment were defective (recall 17V-609, 2015-2016 Lancers and 2015 Evolutions).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the relays free.

issues.sym: The car hesitates or is slow to pick up speed when you press the gas.
issues.why: CVT control software could delay acceleration in some conditions (recall 16V-563).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer reprograms the CVT computer free.

issues.sym: A squeak or chirp from the engine bay that is worse on cold mornings and changes with engine speed.
issues.why: The automatic belt tensioner weakens and lets the serpentine belt slip.
issues.next: Replace the tensioner and belt together. Check first for the belt recalls on 2008-2012 cars.

issues.t: Stalling from dirty throttle body or bad MAP sensor
issues.sym: The engine stalls when pulling away or while cruising, often with no warning light or code.
issues.why: A clogged throttle body or a failing manifold pressure (MAP) sensor can confuse the engine computer.
issues.next: Have the throttle body cleaned and the MAP sensor checked with live data. Also make sure the relay recall on 2015-2016 cars is done.

issues.t: Exhaust leak at the front pipe gasket
issues.sym: A louder exhaust or a ticking or puffing sound, especially when cold.
issues.why: The ceramic donut gasket between the exhaust manifold and down pipe wears and leaks.
issues.next: Have the joint inspected and the gasket, bolts and springs replaced.

issues.sym: The car drifts or pulls, usually to the left, even after tire rotations or alignments.
issues.why: Owners report persistent pulling, especially on all-wheel-drive cars; factory alignment settings are often off.
issues.next: Get a full four-wheel alignment from a shop experienced with these cars and check tire wear and pressures.
